quote: Proposition 2.1 Let T1, T2, . . . , Tn denote the component lifetimes of a series (parallel) system and let relative error in SF due to faulty assumption of components independently working in the series (parallel) system be denoted by ESF(t) (EPF(t)). Then (i) OA(UA) in error assessment of SF for an n component series system is equivalent to the fact that T1, T2, . . . , Tn are PUOD (NUOD). (ii) OA(UA) in error assessment of SF for an n component parallel system is equivalent to the fact that T1, T2, . . . , Tn are PLOD (NLOD).

quote: Remark 2.2 (i) The over-assessment and under-assessment of a reliability function (say SF, FR, RFR, MRL, AI) are basically the study of the stochastic ordering (respectively, usual stochastic order, FR order, RFR order, MRL order, AI order, respectively) among the corresponding function between the dependent and independent counterpart of the system concerned. Mathematically, we express as, let TD and TI represent the lifetime of the series system formed by n dependent and independent components respectively. Clearly, TD ≤ST (≥ST)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in SF. So is for orders based on FR, MRL, RFR, AI, i.e., TD ≤FR (≥FR)TI if and only if there is UA (OA) in FR., TD ≤MRL (≥MRL)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in MRL., TD ≤RFR (≥RFR)TI if and only if there is OA (UA) in RFR., TD ≤AI (≥AI)TI if and only if there is UA (OA) in AI.
